## What it is

Before the capstone, there was a much smaller question: does the speed of
an incoming ball predict how accurately a player returns it? For DATA 152,
I tracked 48 shots and looked for a relationship between incoming ball
speed and shot accuracy.

## What I did

- Manually recorded incoming ball speed and shot outcome for 48 tennis
  groundstrokes.
- Built a small analysis in R to test for a relationship between speed and
  accuracy.
- Used the result, and its limitations, to scope a much larger follow-up
  study.

## The result

The sample was too small to draw a confident conclusion, but the exercise
surfaced the real question worth answering: not just "does incoming speed
matter," but "what actually predicts accuracy, and can I measure accuracy
well enough to find out." That question became the foundation of my
capstone, [Quantifying the Court](/capstone.qmd), which scaled this idea up
to 1,072 shots with a proper weighted scoring system.
